question_text: Find the equation of the plane passing through the point (−2, 1, 3) and having (3, −5, 4) as the direction ratios of its normal.

recall_prompt: Say how you would solve this — say what the direction ratios of the normal give you, and which form of the plane equation you write.

steps.label: Write the point-and-normal form
steps.margin_note: First mark. A point on the plane and the direction ratios of its normal fix the plane completely, and the point-and-normal form uses both at once.
steps.memory_tip: The normal's direction ratios ARE the coefficients of x, y and z in the plane equation.
lines: The plane through (x₁, y₁, z₁) whose normal
has direction ratios (a, b, c) is
a(x − x₁) + b(y − y₁) + c(z − z₁) = 0

recall.must_convey: That the point-and-normal form a(x − x₁) + b(y − y₁) + c(z − z₁) = 0 is written with the given point and the given normal ratios.
accept: use a into x minus x one plus b into y minus y one plus c into z minus z one equals zero
the normal's direction ratios are the coefficients
a point and a normal fix the plane
point and normal form rasi values pettali
write the point and normal form first
reject: expand the brackets and collect the constants
heard_as: a into x minus x one

steps.why: Every point of the plane makes a line with (x₁, y₁, z₁) that is perpendicular to the normal, and that perpendicular condition written out is exactly this equation.
common_mistakes: Swapping the point and the normal ratios in the formula.
Using the direction ratios of a line lying in the plane instead of the normal's.

steps.label: Substitute and simplify
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The point has a negative coordinate, so x − (−2) becomes x + 2. Expand all three brackets, then collect the constants and check the point satisfies the answer.
steps.memory_tip: x − (−2) becomes x + 2 — a negative coordinate flips the sign inside the bracket.

recall.must_convey: That expanding gives 3x − 5y + 4z − 1 = 0, and that the given point satisfies it.

the plane is three x minus five y plus four z minus one equals zero

steps.why: The coefficients must come out unchanged as 3, −5 and 4, because only the constant term depends on which point the plane passes through. Substituting the point back is the quick test that the constant is right.
common_mistakes: Writing 3(x − 2) instead of 3(x + 2) for the negative coordinate.
Adding the constants wrongly and getting +1 in place of −1.
